title: Remarks at Marshall, North Carolina
paragraphs: It is a great pleasure to me to have the chance of greeting you this morning. Late last evening I received a telegram from Senator Pritchard, saying I must surely stop, if only for a moment, at Marshall. I have been admiring greatly your beautiful scenery coming through this morning. I am glad to see the mountains and the rivers, but I am gladder still to see you.(Applause) I have just been down to a meeting at Chattanooga of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen. I have always greatly respected the railroad men, because they have certain qualities that I regard as essential to good citizenship.

It always has seemed to me a good thing for the President to visit the different parts of the country, if only to find out that a good American is a good American wherever he is; and it is of very little consequence whether it is north or south or east or west, if he is a square man and a decent citizen.(Applause)
